body, report it; then name the player your evidence most points to — someone you
saw near the body, on an odd path, or whose account does not fit yours.

## What to do
Decide who is most likely the impostor and commit to it. The crew catches the
impostor by establishing who was WHERE and WHEN, so put the sightings that matter
on the record as structured `saw_player` observations (player, room, tick, and who

in MEDBAY." — ALWAYS put it on the record as a structured `saw_vent`
observation, copying the player, room, and tick from that line exactly: only
the impostor can vent, so one witnessed vent identifies the impostor outright

discards your whole turn. Then either name your single best suspect in one

Output exactly one JSON object matching the `MeetingTurn` schema — nothing else.

and NO others:
`turn_id`, `turn_index`, `speaker`, `turn_kind`, `reply_to`, `observations`,
`claims`, `free_text`.
There is NO top-level `type` key — a `type` field appears ONLY inside each
`observations` / `claims` item (its discriminator), never on the turn itself.

The first five are identity fields the meeting system overwrites after parsing, but
each is still REQUIRED — omitting one fails validation. Emit them as:
- `turn_id`: any non-empty string (e.g. `"t"`).
- `turn_index`: any integer (e.g. `0`).
- `speaker`: `"p-3"`.
- `turn_kind`: the string `"opening"`.
- `reply_to`: `null`.

Content fields (your real turn):
- `observations`: first-hand things you saw, each item one of these shapes (each carries its own `type`):
  - `{"type": "saw_player", "tick": <int>, "subject": "<player_id>", "room": "<room_id>", "co_present": ["<player_id>", ...]}`
  - `{"type": "completed_task", "tick": <int>, "task_id": "<task_id>", "room": "<room_id>"}`
  - `{"type": "found_body", "tick": <int>, "body_of": "<player_id>", "room": "<room_id>"}`
  - `{"type": "saw_vent", "tick": <int>, "subject": "<player_id>", "room": "<room_id>"}` — ONLY
